observations.text: Reassessment scope, mechanically selected at 1329db8 with a clean tree (git status --porcelain empty, exit 0): git diff --stat 13eaef8 HEAD -- crates/foundry-app/tests docs/feature/iis-secrets-key-replace/acceptance.md (exit 0) returns 2 files, 201 insertions, 0 deletions - the new support crates/foundry-app/tests/iis_secrets_key_bound.rs (164 lines, one generated test) and S2 row 11 of acceptance.md (37 lines). git diff --stat 13eaef8 HEAD over the whole range also shows production and design files (secrets_key_rotation.rs, instance.rs, reload.rs, worker.rs, architecture.md, ADR-IIS-SKR-004, the Quint model and other runs records); none of those is judged here. Only the new support and row 11 are reassessed; every prior judgment of this oracle at 5735cda is retained, including S2 rows 1-10.

Semantic RED of the delta, from the supplied run only: argv timeout -k 30 590 scripts/test-in-lima.sh cargo test -p foundry-app --test iis_secrets_key_bound, exit 101, 1 test run with 0 passed and 1 failed, finished in 0.00s. The failure is the promised refusal, not a setup defect: foundry-app compiled in 12.50s and the target ran, and the panic at iis_secrets_key_bound.rs:88 is the test's own WHAT/WHY/HOW message 'a Foundry asked to reload every 20001 ms refuses to start ... Refuse the setting where it is read, with no settings value produced', shrunk to the minimal failing input Milliseconds(20001) with 0 local and 0 global rejects. So the checkpoint that fails is exactly the L14 bound and nothing else.

The RED holds on the judged bytes without a second execution, and no lane was run in this round. The run the root cites is at this same commit 1329db8, and the outcome depends only on the test's own bytes and on crates/foundry-app/src/integrations/config.rs: git diff --stat 13eaef8 HEAD -- crates/foundry-app/src/integrations/config.rs is empty (exit 0), and at HEAD line 271 still reads reload: Duration::from_millis(whole_number(&get, RELOAD_MS, DEFAULT_RELOAD_MS)?.max(1)) with no envelope check and no new ConfigError variant, so 20001 ms is still admitted and read_with(Milliseconds(20001)) still returns Ok where the test requires an error. The refused side carries 6 of the 14 generator weights over 256 cases, so a refused value is reached with certainty. Nothing is restamped as a new execution.

The support drives the public port the design names and declares every input it depends on. It imports only foundry_app::integrations::config::{ConfigError, IntegrationSettings, DEFAULT_RELOAD_MS, RELOAD_MS}, all pub at config.rs:38,43,71 and 250, and calls IntegrationSettings::from_lookup with a lookup closure of its own that answers only RELOAD_MS, as eip_phase5_doors.rs does. No std::env::set_var, no filesystem, no clock and no network, so the test reads no ambient state, cannot collide with a parallel target and passes alone. It is a cargo integration target under crates/foundry-app/tests, auto-discovered by the declared command and by the gate, which runs cargo test --workspace excluding foundry-acceptance (xtask/src/main.rs:195,287), so no registration is needed and the target cannot be silently skipped. 256 cases of pure parsing finished in 0.00s, far inside budget; no timing measurement was required or claimed.

Closure of row 11 in both directions, and the oracle stays independent of the code under test. Forward: L14 and T7 require that every value to 20000 is admitted and read as given, unset reads as the 5000 ms default, 0 reads as 1 ms, every larger value is refused where the setting is read with no settings value produced, the refusal names the setting, the value and the bound, and a non-numeric value is still refused as not a number. The generator covers all of it - Nothing, four non-numeric texts, 0, 1, ENVELOPE_MS, ENVELOPE_MS+1, 60000, u64::MAX, plus the full ranges 1..=20000 and 20001..=u64::MAX - and the match arms assert each outcome, so both edges of the boundary are pinned by explicit cases and an off-by-one bound that refused 20000 would fail. Backward: the test asserts nothing without authority; the only other value it supplies, PUBLIC_URL, is incidental setup and is never asserted. The bound is its own constant ENVELOPE_MS = 20_000, worked out from ADR-IIS-SKR-004 and never read back from the production constant the craft will add, so a craft that set a different envelope cannot make this test agree with it.

No incidental coupling, and the overlap with the shipped config table is bounded and purposeful. The new refusal is observed only through the public error's own words - said.contains(RELOAD_MS), the value, and the bound as 20000 or '20 s' - so craft may name the new ConfigError variant anything, while the non-numeric case keeps matching the shipped public variant ConfigError::NotANumber { setting } so an out-of-range refusal cannot masquerade as a parse refusal. Four of the test's branches restate cases the shipped unit table at config.rs:547-581 already observes by example (unset to default, '0' to 1 ms, 'soon' to NotANumber); that table also keeps observations this property does not carry, the blank and whitespace readings, and the property's admitted side is what makes its refused side a partition rather than a one-sided claim, so the property adds the universal law the table cannot state. No consolidation is owed to this oracle, and config.rs is not its file.

Authority and scope of row 11 as recorded. ADR-IIS-SKR-004 is Accepted with decisions D11 and D12, the design review accepted the from_lookup locator at 3760ba7, and architecture.md ties the bound to P6: above the 20 s envelope a server leaves more than the 40 s window between two of its own beats, is read as gone, and Start over is offered while it still serves with the credentials (Y11). So the bound is the enabling condition of the promise this slice already owns, not a new requirement, and the row covers P6 rather than widening scope. The deliberate breaking change K6 is documented prose-only in RELEASING.md:382 and docs/product/architecture/brief.md:1221, and the row's own falsifier text delegates that wording to review and the examiner; no test pins the prose, which is what the test-design mandate on documentation requires.
